item.title: Daily and weekly reminders know when to pause
item.summary: When an ordinary daily or weekly reminder receives no reply, Murph now asks once whether to keep, change, or pause it instead of repeating indefinitely.
item.details: If that question also goes unanswered, later ordinary reminders stay quiet until someone replies about the reminder or asks Murph to resume or change it. A longer cadence or unusual delay continues the cue when its prior delivery evidence has expired, rather than guessing from missing context. In groups, Murph asks the room and never blames a participant. Medication, clinician-directed, and safety-critical reminders keep sending unless explicitly changed or paused.
